title: Israeli Video Games Industry Report
publisher: Deloitte Israel and Start-Up Nation Central
methodology: Primary Israeli-industry source: public Start-Up Nation Finder data; additional GameIS/affiliate information. Dataset intentionally includes companies with target markets beyond video games and supporting technology/services; Deloitte calls findings preliminary and says it did not independently verify inputs.
assessment: Primary predecessor and source of approximately 4,000-worker headline. Retain as contextual Israeli-company ecosystem mapping, not domestic workers/FTEs. Its social-casino inclusion is stated to exclude monetary payouts.
access_status: downloaded and text-extracted; primary excerpts retained in findings.md
next_step: Locate underlying Finder snapshot or company-level Israel-site headcounts before using as domestic employment.

title: The Israeli Video Games Ecosystem: Converging Technologies, Emerging Opportunities
methodology: Employment total methodology is not stated. Selected-company source note cites Start-Up Nation, Crunchbase, Pitchbook and company websites. Market-size calculation is described, but it is not an employment method.
assessment: Primary GameIS/Deloitte successor. Provides 4,000/14,000 comparison but mixes publishers/developers with supporting tech and profiles global companies/workforces; worker geography unresolved. Includes 888, so real-money scope is not clean.
access_status: downloaded and text-extracted; primary excerpts retained in findings.md
next_step: Request GameIS/Deloitte company roster, respondent frame, Israel-based worker counts and RMG flag.

title: Israeli Game Companies Survey 2022
methodology: Partner-assisted directory/survey. It says 'Nobody knows the exact number' and gives rough company counts by type (170+ publishers/developers, 100+ marketing, about 90 other gaming-related).
assessment: Useful forward-trace negative result: broad company universe, no total employment headcount and no domestic-worker measurement.
next_step: Do not infer employment; use only if a named partner provides its underlying roster and worker-location fields.

title: Standard Classification of Economic Activities 2011
methodology: Official industrial classification. Class 5820 software publishing includes computer games on all platforms, operating systems and business/other applications; excludes software development (6201) and hosting (6311).
assessment: Official definitional evidence only. It proves an available broad classification, not a games-sector employment series, and would omit much development/support work in the GameIS/Deloitte ecosystem.
next_step: Query CBS for a 5820 employment series only if it is explicitly labelled as broad software publishing, never as games employment.

title: CBS API Interface
methodology: Official portal describes a central time-series database covering employment and business subjects; no games-specific headcount was found in the bounded search.
assessment: Negative official-source result. Do not replace missing games data with CBS high-tech/ICT totals.
next_step: Contact CBS or inspect table catalog for a released 5820 series and document coverage if found.

title: Innovation in Israel 2022: Situation Report, Part A
methodology: Official high-tech situation report using broad CBS/high-tech categories.
assessment: Negative official-source result for this archive: broad high-tech employment is not an explicit games-industry headcount and must not be used as a proxy.
next_step: Exclude from games employment series; retain only as broad economy context if separately needed.
